title: Find the Hot Gate
lesson: Where you place a check can matter more than how many checks you use.
brief: This four-qubit GHZ circuit has one CNOT that is much noisier than the others. Its error-rate badge is highlighted. You have one check, so choose its span carefully.
learning_moment: The goal is not to cover every gate equally. A check is valuable when it can flag the errors that are likely to happen. Here, covering the highlighted CNOT is more useful than spending the check on a group of comparatively reliable gates. Read the error-rate badges, then compare your Fidelity and Yield with a check placed elsewhere.
hint: Find the CNOT with the orange error-rate badge first. Try a check that covers it, then try one somewhere else and compare.
reflection: Did covering the hottest gate help more than covering several quieter gates?
noise_note: One two-qubit gate is much noisier than the others; look for its highlighted error-rate badge.

noise.label: level noise with one hot CNOT (q2-q3)

explanation: One CNOT, between q2 and q3, is much noisier than the rest (the orange badge).
A Z check on q2 from slot 2 covers the last two CNOTs, including the hot one. It ends at the readout as Z on q1 and q2, asking whether q1 and q2 still agree.
A check on the quiet CNOTs instead watches errors that rarely happen, so it gains much less.
